'''Anthony M. Bloch''' is an American [[mathematician]] and the Alexander Ziwet Collegiate Professor of Mathematics at the [[University of Michigan]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite journal |last1=Leonardo |first1=Colombo |last2=Manuel |first2=de León |last3=Tomoki |first3=Ohsawa |date=2021-03-01 |title=Preface to the special issue dedicated to Anthony Bloch |url=https://www.aimsciences.org/en/article/doi/10.3934/jgm.2021004 |journal=Journal of Geometric Mechanics |language=en |volume=13 |issue=1 |pages=i–iii |doi=10.3934/jgm.2021004 |issn=1941-4889|doi-access=free }}</ref>

He is known for his contributions to [[Hamiltonian mechanics|Hamiltonian]] and [[Lagrangian mechanics]], geometric control theory, [[integrable system]]s, and nonholonomic mechanics.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Anthony Bloch |url=https://www.icmat.es/congresos/2023/BLOCHFEST/ |website=[[Institute of Mathematical Sciences (Spain)]]}}</ref> He has held editorial positions and served three terms as Chair of the [[University of Michigan]] Department of Mathematics.<ref name=":1">https://lsa.umich.edu/content/dam/math-assets/math-document/continuum/summer2005.pdf

Anthony Bloch Named Chair</ref>

In 2012 he was named a [[Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics|Fellow of Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics]]<ref name=":2">{{Cite web |title=Anthony Bloch named a Fellow of the Society of Industrial and Applied Mathematics (SIAM) {{!}} U-M LSA Mathematics |url=https://lsa.umich.edu/math/news-events/all-news/archived-news/2013/03/anthony-bloch-named-a-fellow-of-the-society-of-industrial-and-ap.html |access-date=2025-09-27 |website=lsa.umich.edu |language=en}}</ref> and a [[American Mathematical Society|Fellow of the American Mathematical Society]].<ref name=":3">{{Cite web |title=AMS :: List of Fellows of the American Mathematical Society |url=https://www.ams.org/grants-awards/fellows-list |access-date=2025-09-27 |website=www.ams.org}}</ref>

He was named a [[Lists of fellows of the IEEE|Fellow of the Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers]] in 2003.<ref name=":4">{{Cite web |title=Fellow of IEEE Anthony Bloch |url=https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/author/37301278800 |access-date=2025-09-27 |website=ieeexplore.ieee.org}}</ref> He is also a [[Guggenheim Fellowship|Guggenheim fellow]]<ref>{{Cite web |title=Anthony M. Bloch Guggenheim Fellowships: Supporting Artists, Scholars, & Scientists |url=https://www.gf.org/fellows/anthony-bloch |access-date=2025-09-27 |website=www.gf.org}}</ref> and Simons Fellows in Mathematics.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2012-06-20 |title=Simons Fellows in Mathematics |url=https://www.simonsfoundation.org/grant/simons-fellows-in-mathematics/ |access-date=2025-09-27 |website=Simons Foundation |language=en-US}}</ref>

== Education ==
Bloch earned a B.Sc. and B.Sc. (Hons.) in Applied Mathematics and Physics from the [[University of the Witwatersrand]] in 1977 and 1978, respectively.<ref name=":5">{{Cite web |last=Baillieul |first=John |title=CISE Seminar: Anthony Bloch, University of Michigan {{!}} Center for Information & Systems Engineering |url=https://www.bu.edu/cise/42580-2/ |access-date=2025-09-27 |website=[[Boston University]]}}</ref> He completed an M.S. in Physics at the [[California Institute of Technology]] in 1979 and an M.Phil. in Control Engineering and Operations Research at the [[University of Cambridge]] in 1981.<ref name=":4" /> In 1985, he received his Ph.D. in Applied Mathematics from [[Harvard University]].<ref name=":5" />

== Career ==
Bloch joined the [[University of Michigan]] faculty in 1985, becoming Alexander Ziwet Collegiate Professor of Mathematics in 2005. He served as Graduate Chair of the Department of Mathematics from 2001 to 2004 and as Department Chair from 2005 to 2008 and again from 2017 to 2023.<ref name=":1" />

He has been a [[Guggenheim Fellow]], Simons Fellow, Senior Fellow of the Michigan Society of Fellows, and is a Life Fellow of the [[Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers]] (IEEE).<ref>{{Cite web |title=Anthony Bloch, the Alexander Ziwet Professor and Head of the Mathematics Department at the University of Michigan, has been elected as a Corresponding Member of NAAI! |url=https://thenaai.org/index/index/newsdata1/id/560.shtml |access-date=2025-09-27 |website=thenaai.org}}</ref>

Bloch is also a Fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]] (AMS),<ref name=":3" /> the [[Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics]] (SIAM),<ref name=":2" /> the [[International Core Academy of Sciences and Humanities]],<ref>{{Cite web |title=Fellows-CORE Academy |url=https://coreacad.org/Fellows.aspx?q1=bloch |access-date=2025-09-27 |website=coreacad.org}}</ref> and a Corresponding Member of the National Academy of Artificial Intelligence.<ref name=":5" />

Bloch has served as Editor-in-Chief of the ''[[Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics|SIAM Journal on Control and Optimization]]'' (2012–2018), Co-Editor-in-Chief of the ''[[Journal of Nonlinear Science]]'' (2018–present), and Book Series Editor for Springer's ''Applied Mathematical Sciences'' series (2018–present).<ref name=":5" />

He was a member of the [[Institute for Advanced Study]] in 1997. In 2023 he was a Distinguished Visiting Professor at the [[Institute of Mathematical Sciences (Spain)|Instituto de Ciencias Matemáticas (ICMAT) in Spain]] and delivered the 30th Annual Owens Lecture at [[Wayne State University]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Anthony Bloch |url=https://www.icmat.es/severo-ochoa/icmat-laboratories/2020-2023/bloch/ |website=ICMAT}}</ref>

== Research ==
Bloch's research spans [[Hamiltonian mechanics|Hamiltonian]] and [[Lagrangian mechanics]], [[symplectic geometry]], geometric [[control theory]], [[Vector field|gradient flows]] on [[manifold]]s, [[integrable system]]s, [[stability theory]], nonholonomic mechanics, [[quantum control]] and [[astrophysics]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Richter |first=Ingrid |title=Anthony Bloch Integrable Hamiltonian and gradient flows and total positivity |url=https://amath.washington.edu/news/2025/03/04/anthony-bloch-integrable-hamiltonian-and-gradient-flows-and-total-positivity |access-date=2025-09-27 |website=[[University of Washington]]}}</ref>

He has worked extensively on the geometric formulation and control of [[nonholonomic system]]s, with influential papers on symmetry reduction and stabilization, and is one of the original developers of the method of controlled Lagrangians.<ref>{{Citation |last=Bloch |first=Anthony M. |chapter=Basic Concepts in Geometric Mechanics |date=2015 |title=Nonholonomic Mechanics and Control |series=Interdisciplinary Applied Mathematics |volume=24 |pages=125–198 |editor-last=Bloch |editor-first=A.M. |place=New York, NY |publisher=Springer |language=en |doi=10.1007/978-1-4939-3017-3_3 |isbn=978-1-4939-3017-3 |editor2-last=Krishnaprasad |editor2-first=P. S. |editor3-last=Murray |editor3-first=R.M.}}</ref>

His research in control theory includes widely cited results with M. Reyhanoglu and N. H. McClamroch on the control of nonholonomic mechanical systems.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Reyhanoglu |first1=Mahmut |last2=Bloch |first2=Anthony M. |last3=Harris Mcclamroch |first3=N. |date=1995 |title=Control of nonholonomic systems with extended base space dynamics |url=https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/abs/10.1002/rnc.4590050408 |journal=International Journal of Robust and Nonlinear Control |language=en |volume=5 |issue=4 |pages=325–330 |doi=10.1002/rnc.4590050408 |issn=1099-1239|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

In integrable systems, Bloch is well known for showing that the Toda lattice flow is gradient on adjoint orbit<ref>https://community.ams.org/journals/bull/1990-23-02/S0273-0979-1990-15960-9/S0273-0979-1990-15960-9.pdf

A new formulation of the generalized toda lattice equations and their fixed point analysis via the momentum map  </ref> and for his work with [[Roger W. Brockett|Roger Brockett]] and [[Tudor Ratiu|Tudor Rațiu]] generalizing this to general Lie algebras as well for his related work on gradient and double bracket flows.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Bloch |first1=Anthony M. |last2=Brockett |first2=Roger W. |last3=Rațiu |first3=Tudor S. | authorlink3=Tudor Ratiu |date=1992-06-01 |title=Completely integrable gradient flows |journal=Communications in Mathematical Physics |language=en |volume=147 |issue=1 |pages=57–74 |doi=10.1007/BF02099528 |bibcode=1992CMaPh.147...57B |issn=1432-0916 |url=http://infoscience.epfl.ch/record/129476 }}</ref>

He also known for work on the symmetric representation of the generalized rigid body equations with Crouch, Marsden, and Rațiu<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Bloch |first1=Anthony M. |last2=Crouch |first2=Peter E. |last3=Marsden |first3=Jerrold E. |last4=Rațiu |first4=Tudor S. | authorlink4=Tudor Ratiu |date=2002 |title=The symmetric representation of the rigid body equations and their discretization |url=http://deepblue.lib.umich.edu/handle/2027.42/49076 |journal=Nonlinearity |language=en-US |volume=4 |issue=15 |hdl=2027.42/49076 |issn=0951-7715}}</ref> and his work with Iserles, Marsden, and Rațiu on  integrable flows on symmetric matrices.<ref>A Class of Integrable Flows on the Space of Symmetric Matrices

https://sites.lsa.umich.edu/abloch/wp-content/uploads/sites/1327/2024/08/BlBrIsMaRa5309_new.pdf</ref>

Bloch is the author of ''Nonholonomic Mechanics and Control'' (now in its second edition), which has been cited over 2,000 times and is regarded as a standard reference in the field.<ref name=":0" /> His most recent book, co-authored with A. Rojo, is ''The Principle of Least Action: History and Physics'', which examines the development and applications of variational principles in mechanics.<ref>{{Cite book |last1=Rojo |first1=Alberto |url=https://www.cambridge.org/core/books/principle-of-least-action/CEDF9D5B2E7ED03F63575F6E11F87BDF |title=The Principle of Least Action: History and Physics |last2=Bloch |first2=Anthony |date=2018 |publisher=Cambridge University Press |isbn=978-0-521-86902-7 |location=Cambridge |doi=10.1017/9781139021029}}</ref>

His recent work also involves data-guided control, network dynamics, and applications to biological systems.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Baillieul Distinguished Lecture Series : Department of Mathematics and Statistics: UMass Amherst |url=https://www.umass.edu/mathematics-statistics/seminars/BDLS |access-date=2025-09-27 |website=www.umass.edu}}</ref> He maintains active collaborations across mathematics, physics, engineering, and applied sciences.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Rand |first=Stephen |title=New research program to investigate optical energy conversion |url=https://ece.engin.umich.edu/stories/new-research-program-to-investigate-optical-energy-conversion/ |access-date=2025-09-27 |website=Electrical and Computer Engineering |language=en-US}}</ref>
